name: Pfunds
kurzbeschreibung: Historic community in the Oberinntal with the famous Pfundser Tschey (sun plateau) and the baroque church.
text:
Overview

Pfunds is located in the Tyrolean Upper Inn Valley in the district of Landeck at an altitude of 971 metres, positioned at the centre of the historic Upper Court region (Oberes Gericht). Situated at the border triangle of Austria, Switzerland, and Italy, this vibrant municipality nestles into the geological Engadine Window where the Inn River forms a dramatic curve. Around 2,600 residents inhabit the town, which is divided by the river into two historic settlements: Pfunds-Dorf on the eastern riverbank and the traditional trading hamlet of Stuben on the western bank, connected by an iconic covered wooden bridge. Picturesque mountain hamlets such as Lafairs, Birkach, and Kobl dot the surrounding slopes. The village architecture is heavily influenced by neighbouring Rhaeto-Romanic Engadine traditions: thick stone masonry, deep funnel-shaped windows, and colourful sgraffito artwork give Pfunds a singular aesthetic. Flanked by the Samnaun Alps and the Ötztal Alps, Pfunds is a prime hub for authentic alpine outdoor recreation.

History

The name Pfunds derives from the Latin fundus, meaning estate or fertile soil; archaeological urn burials confirm human presence dating back 3,000 years. The community was first documented in 1282 as judicium Phundes and retained its own district court until 1809. A remarkable landmark of medieval fortified architecture is the Turm am Rain (locally called Turaloch) at the bridgehead: originating in the 11th century, this residential tower was reinforced in 1499 under Emperor Maximilian I during the Engadine War; today, the public road still passes directly through its vaulted gateway. A few kilometres upriver on the Roman Via Claudia Augusta lies the fortress of Altfinstermünz: documented as early as 1078, the gorge fortification was expanded after 1472 by Archduke Sigmund the Wealthy and Maximilian I with a bridge tower, the Siegmundsegg redoubt, and a cave fortress. The late Gothic Church of Our Lady in Stuben houses an exquisite carved winged altarpiece by master Jörg Lederer dating from 1513.

Getting There

Pfunds enjoys excellent transport connections at an international alpine crossroads. Motorists travelling from Innsbruck take the Inntal Autobahn A12 through the Landeck Tunnel onto the Reschen federal road B180, reaching Pfunds in approximately one hour; from Italy, the route traverses the Reschen Pass, while travellers from Switzerland take the Engadine Highway via Martinsbruck directly into town. Rail passengers arrive at Landeck-Zams station on the Arlberg Railway, served regularly by international ÖBB Railjet trains. From the station forecourt, VVT regional bus route 210 operates frequent direct services reaching Pfunds centre in around 45 minutes. Regular bus connections also serve the Swiss duty-free resort of Samnaun and neighbouring Nauders.

Tips

The crown jewel of nature is the Pfundser Tschey, a high-altitude plateau at 1,650 metres in the Radurschl Valley: this protected landscape features over 400 rustic timber hay barns, the Chapel of Maria Schnee, a spectacular sea of purple crocuses in spring, and idyllic snowshoeing and cross-country ski trails in winter. History lovers must explore Altfinstermünz, accessed by an inclined cliff lift, featuring the restored bridge tower and border museum over the churning river. Hikers can trek through the rugged Radurschl Gorge across suspension bridges up to the Hohenzollernhaus hut (2,120 m). Experienced climbers tackle the Anton Renk via ferrata alongside a thundering waterfall, while archery enthusiasts enjoy the year-round 3D archery park at Tschingls.
